title: Going to Los Angeles in 1919 with Ory's group
summary: Williams went west with Ory's men, stayed on after the band broke up, and recalls arriving in October in a straw hat; they played the Cadillac.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: You mentioned then when you went to California, were there any other bands before you went out there, though, that you can tell us about that you played with?

No, I went out there with O'Rell. I didn't play with nobody but O'Rell. No, I didn't play with nobody but O'Rell. After the band broke up, well they raid the nightclubs, wherever that's so much, you know, and the bands broke up. And I got a job working for the railroad, working cleaning cars for the South Pacific a while. O'Rell, O'Rell, Wade, and Mutt, a guy taking them to Los Angeles, I don't know whether it was Los Angeles or Frisco, a guy that called Curtis Molesby. I guess you heard of him out there. He had nightclubs and everything after that, you know. Well, he take an O'Rell, and Wade Whaley to Frisco while I stayed in Los Angeles.
I was waiting for the railroad there and got my job waiting for the railroad there. So you stayed out there there? A while.

I stayed out there from 19 from October. I must have got in Los Angeles from 1919 by October the first or second. And it was the funnest thing when I got off the train I had on a straw hat in October. And I guess the people out there was looking at me, you know, well it was hot just like it is this year when I left. And we got off the train I had a straw hat on. I felt so embarrassed and ashamed. That's a warm air chair though. Yes indeed, having a straw hat on. We played at the Cadillac in Los Angeles, I guess Manuel told you that.
